title: "About"

## Background

I am a public health researcher, biostatistician, and data analyst with over seven years of experience 
spanning global health communication, program evaluation, and AI-assisted research. My career has been 
built at Vital Strategies, where I have progressed from research intern to consultant, leading 
multi-country research and evaluation projects across five continents.

My work sits at the intersection of public health evidence generation and data science. I apply 
advanced statistical methods, machine learning tools, and real-time data systems to evaluate how 
health communication campaigns change behavior, how commercial actors market harmful products online, 
and how public health evidence can be translated into policy and practice.

## Research Interests

- **Commercial determinants of health** — surveillance of tobacco, alcohol, and ultra-processed food 
  marketing; digital marketing monitoring; policy evaluation
- **Overdose prevention and harm reduction** — campaign evaluation; behavioral determinants of 
  naloxone uptake; stigma measurement
- **AI in public health research** — large language model classification; explainable AI; automated 
  content analysis; digital surveillance systems
- **Health communication and campaign evaluation** — Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) 
  frameworks; multi-stream data integration; behavioral prediction modeling
- **Global nutrition policy** — front-of-package labeling; sugary drinks taxation; ultra-processed 
  food regulation

## Approach

I believe rigorous methods and accessible communication are equally important. My analytical work 
combines advanced statistical modeling with practical tools — automated dashboards, reproducible 
Python workflows, and AI-assisted validation systems — that make research faster, more transparent, 
and more useful to the people who need it.

I work across quantitative and qualitative traditions, from survey-weighted logistic regression and 
structural equation modeling to qualitative message testing and systematic review. I am particularly 
interested in how AI tools can augment, rather than replace, human analytical judgment in complex 
public health research contexts.
